rounds.title: Avatar baseline
rounds.note: First drawing of the SDK avatar (et-avatar) and avatar group (et-avatar-group), drawn by their mock from @ethlete/components/design on the page: image, initials (derived or explicit), a projected etIcon and the empty fallback, on a full-opacity primary fill with on-primary text; five sizes (xs 24px to xl 64px), circle and square (8px radius); the inherited colour theme (brand in this product) and the brand, warning and danger themes; the group with its 8px overlap, 2px surface-background ring and +N overflow avatar. The avatar has no hover, active or focus states of its own (a link or button avatar keeps the consumer element), so Q88 (focus rings) and Q101 (filled hover) do not apply; the lib has no status dot, so there is none to measure. Today on light the mint fill vanishes against the page: 1.33:1 with no edge (warning 3.19:1, danger 4.83:1). Dark: mint 13.50:1, warning 5.63:1, danger 3.71:1. Fixed numbers: initials on their fill 15.82:1 mint, 5.63:1 warning, 4.83:1 danger in both schemes; the projected icon in on-primary on mint 15.82:1; the group ring is the page colour, so it separates neighbours, not the avatar from the page. Not this round's question: the projected etIcon has no size inside the avatar, so its SVG fills the whole 40px box and is clipped (it reads as a black disc with a mint glyph; the lib needs an icon size rule); the danger fill against the dark page (3.71:1); the xs initials at 10px; the image form's numbers (the placeholder portrait is a generic drawing); pane edges (Q98, open). Variants b and c apply decided rule Q99 rule a: avatars that show a fill (initials, icon, empty, +N) get a 1px inset ink edge, drawn as an outline with a -1px offset so it neither changes the size nor fights the group's box-shadow ring; image avatars keep no edge. Variant a shows today.

a.note: Today: on light the mint fill is 1.33:1 against the page with no edge (warning 3.19:1, danger 4.83:1). Dark: mint 13.50:1, warning 5.63:1, danger 3.71:1. Initials 15.82:1 / 5.63:1 / 4.83:1 on their fill in both schemes.

b.note: Pick. Decided rule Q99 rule a: every fill avatar takes a 1px inset --et-theme-color-ink-solid edge (outline, offset -1px). Light: edge 5.48:1 against the page (warning 7.09:1, danger 6.47:1), against the mint fill 4.13:1 (warning 2.23:1, danger 1.34:1). Dark: ink is mint, so the edge is invisible on the mint fill and draws 8.35:1 (warning) and 6.48:1 (danger) against the page, a lighter ring around those fills (1.48:1 and 1.75:1 against them). Picked to match the badge round's pick: ink follows the scheme, so the edge runs in both. Q102 (does the ink edge also show in dark?) is open; if dark should stay as today, take c. Beyond rule a: the edge also lands on warning and danger, not only mint.

c.note: b with the ink edge on light only: the outline takes light-dark(ink, transparent). Light equal to b (edge 5.48:1 against the page, 4.13:1 against the mint fill); dark as today (mint 13.50:1, warning 5.63:1, danger 3.71:1, no edge). It keys on color-scheme, not on the surface, so a dark surface theme inside a light page would still draw the edge; that mechanism is my reading of rule a, not a decided rule (Q102).
